document.title: Limited Protest of American Municipal Power, Inc. to PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.'s 08/17/2026 Compliance Filing

pages.text:
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA 
BEFORE THE 
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. 
) 
Docket No. ER26-1479-002 
LIMITED PROTEST OF 
AMERICAN MUNICIPAL POWER, INC. 
American Municipal Power, Inc. (“AMP”) hereby protests the August 17, 2026 
compliance filing by PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) in the above-captioned docket,1
in which PJM proposes revisions to its Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”) to 
comply with directives in the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission” or 
“FERC”) June 18, 2026 order in Docket Nos. EL25-49-002, et al.2 As discussed below, 
AMP’s protest is limited to one aspect of the PJM Filing: the proposed definition for Eligible 
Generating Facility is too narrow.3
I. 
BACKGROUND AND INTRODUCTION 
Historically, the PJM Tariff allowed load served by Behind the Meter Generation 
(“BTMG”) to be netted from daily load under sections 34.2 and 34.3 of the PJM Tariff for 
purposes of calculating charges for Network Integration Transmission Service and other 
PJM charges.4 AMP and AMP’s load-serving utility members own and operate generating 
1
PJM, Compliance Filing in Response to Order on Rehearing, Clarification, Compliance Filing, and Paper 
Hearing in Docket Nos. EL25-49-002, et al., Docket No. ER26-1479-002 (Aug. 17, 2026) (“PJM Filing”). 
2
PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 195 FERC ¶ 61,209 (2026) (“June 18 Order”).  
3
See PJM Filing, Transmittal Letter at 13; id. at Attachment A, proposed Tariff, Part I, section 1 
(Definitions E – F). 
4
See generally, PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 193 FERC ¶ 61,217, at P 7 (2025) (“December 18 
Order”).The definition of BTMG, as previously proposed by PJM, is as follows (pending new language 
underlined): 
“Behind The Meter Generation” shall mean either Retail Behind the Meter 
Generation or Non-Retail Behind The Meter Generation and refers to a generation 
unit that delivers energy to load without using the Transmission System or any 
distribution facilities (unless the entity that owns or leases the distribution facilities

2 
units in the PJM region that qualified (and continue to qualify) as “Non-Retail BTMG” – a 
distinct category of BTMG subject to certain specific conditions and limitations.5
In the December 18 Order,6 the Commission drew a distinction between “retail” 
BTMG and Non-Retail BTMG, and concluded that PJM’s rules allowing netting of retail 
BTMG were no longer just and reasonable.7 The Commission directed PJM to revise the 
Tariff provisions addressing certain generating units that are classified as retail BTMG.8
The Commission made clear, however, that it was not directing PJM to make any changes 
to its rules for Non-Retail BTMG.9 PJM’s February 23, 2026 compliance filing proposed 
numerous Tariff changes in response to these directives, including, inter alia, the new 
defined term “Retail Behind The Meter Generation.”10
has consented to such use of the distribution facilities and such consent has been 
demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Office of the Interconnection); provided, 
however, that Behind The Meter Generation does not include (i) at any time, any 
portion of such generating unit’s capacity that is designated as a Generation 
Capacity Resource or DER Capacity Aggregation Resource; or (ii) in an hour, any 
portion of the output of such generating unit that is sold to another entity for 
consumption at another electrical location or into the PJM Interchange Energy 
Market. 
PJM Filing, Attachment A (proposed Tariff, Part I, section 1 (Definitions A – B). 
5  Non-Retail Behind the Meter Generation is defined in the Tariff as “Behind the Meter Generation that is 
used by municipal electric systems, electric cooperatives, or electric distribution companies to serve 
load.” Tariff, Part I, section 1 (Definitions L – M – N); see also PJM Filing, Attachment A, proposed Tariff, 
section 34.3. 
6  193 FERC ¶ 61,217. 
7
See id. PP 179, 186. 
8
Id. PP 186, 221-224. Specifically, the Commission directed PJM to “propose a new [megawatt] threshold 
for the amount of load at a particular electrical location that Network Customers may net by using 
BTMG.” Id. P 221. Recognizing that customers may have relied on the existing BTMG rules, however, 
the Commission required PJM to maintain the current BTMG rules for customers that fall below the new 
megawatt threshold level. See id. P 179. The Commission also adopted a transition process for “retail 
BTMG,” including a three-year transition period and grandfathering of certain parties with existing 
contracts. See id. 
9
See id. P 222.  
10  PJM proposed defining Retail Behind The Meter Generation as: “Behind The Meter Generation that is 
used to serve a retail load served by a Network Customer located at the same electrical location (not 
including back-up generation at the same electrical location as the retail load that can only be used to

3 
In the June 18 Order, the Commission set aside the December 18 Order, in part, 
concluding that “the Tariff is unjust and unreasonable because it does not include 
transmission services that reflect that Eligible Customers taking transmission service on 
behalf of load with BTMG are willing and able to limit their energy withdrawals from the 
transmission system under certain conditions.”11 The Commission indicated that it would 
be unjust and unreasonable to require Eligible Customers taking transmission service on 
behalf of load with BTMG to take Network Integration Transmission Service (“NITS”), 
without the option to instead take the alternative transmission services that FERC 
adopted in the December 18 Order for Eligible Customers taking transmission service on 
behalf of Co-Located Load.12
To address these concerns, the Commission introduced the term “Eligible Load,” 
and specified that the term “refer[s] to Co-Located Load and/or load with BTMG.”13 The 
Commission directed PJM to file “a definition for Eligible Load, or other comparable Tariff 
revisions to implement” FERC’s directives.14 Further, the Commission specified that PJM 
must “revise its definition of BTMG to allow Eligible Customers taking transmission 
service on behalf of load with BTMG that are willing and able to limit their energy 
withdrawals from the transmission system under certain conditions to take the new 
transmission services, consistent with this order.”15
serve such retail load during conditions that may threaten the integrity or reliability of the PJM Region 
or the regional power system).” PJM Filing, Attachment A (proposed Tariff, Part I, section 1 (Definitions 
R – S). 
11  June 18 Order at P 91. 
12 See id. 
13 Id. (footnotes omitted).  
14 Id. 
15 Id.

4 
In response to these directives, PJM proposes to amend the Tariff to add Eligible 
Load as a defined term.16 PJM also proposes to add the term “Eligible Generating 
Facility,” which PJM says would “encompass both a Co-Located Generating Facility or 
Retail BTMG.”17 Further, PJM offers a number of other conforming changes to the Tariff 
to reflect the adoption of these new definitions.18
AMP supports the Commission’s decision to extend eligibility for the new 
transmission services to Eligible Customers taking transmission service on behalf of load 
with BTMG. AMP is concerned, however, that PJM’s proposed Tariff provisions – 
particularly the proposed definition of “Eligible Generating Facility” and related conforming 
changes could limit eligibility for the new transmission services in contravention of the 
Commission’s June 18 Order. 
II. 
PROTEST 
A. 
The Commission should direct PJM to revise the proposed definition 
of Eligible Generating Facility because it could exclude otherwise 
eligible Non-Retail BTMG from taking new transmission services. 
The PJM Filing proposes to define Eligible Load as “Co-Located Load or load 
connected to Behind the Meter Generation.”19 This definition appears to comply with the 
Commission’s directives in the June 18 Order inasmuch as it would encompass all “load 
16 See PJM Filing, Transmittal Letter at 13 (citing proposed Tariff, Part I, section 1 (Definitions E - F)).  
17 Id.
18 See id. at 13-14. Separately, the PJM Filing removes PJM’s proposed changes to the definition of Non-
Retail BTMG that the Commission rejected in the June 18 Order. See June 18 Order at P 314; see also 
PJM Filing, Transmittal Letter at 22. 
19  PJM Filing, Attachment A, proposed Tariff, Part I, section 1 (Definitions E - F).

5 
with BTMG,”20 because the Tariff defines BTMG to include both Retail and Non-Retail 
BTMG.21
PJM’s proposed definition of Eligible Generating Facility, however, excludes 
generators serving as Non-Retail BTMG: “‘Eligible Generating Facility’ shall mean a Co-
Located Generating Facility or Retail Behind the Meter Generation.”22 PJM’s Transmittal 
Letter does not explain why an Eligible Generating Facility is defined only with reference 
to Retail BTMG, rather than to all BTMG (including Non-Retail BTMG), or how such a 
limitation complies with the directives in the June 18 Order. The Commission was clear 
that the new transmission services should be available to “Eligible Customers taking 
transmission service on behalf of load with BTMG.”23 The Commission did not distinguish 
between Retail and Non-Retail BTMG, and specifically cited to the general definition of 
BTMG in the Tariff.24 Indeed, the Commission did not require PJM to adopt a definition of 
Eligible Generating Facility at all; it directed PJM “to revise its definition of BTMG to allow 
Eligible Customers taking transmission service on behalf of load with BTMG” to take the 
new transmission services.25 Even if PJM had the latitude to add a new definition for 
20 See June 18 Order at P 91. 
21 See Tariff, Part I, section 1 (Definitions A - B) (specifying in part that “‘Behind The Meter Generation’ 
shall mean either Retail Behind the Meter Generation or Non-Retail Behind The Meter Generation . . .”); 
see also supra note 4. 
22  PJM Filing, Attachment A, proposed Tariff, Part I, section 1 (Definitions E - F) (emphasis added). 
23  June 18 Order at P 91.  
24 See id. P 91 n.217 (cross-referencing footnote 4 of the June 18 Order which quoted the general definition 
of BTMG). 
25 Id. P 91 (emphasis added).

6 
Eligible Generating Facility in its compliance filing,26 PJM has not adequately explained 
why the term excludes Non-Retail BTMG.  
As noted above, AMP and AMP’s load-serving utility members own and operate 
generating units in the PJM region that qualify as Non-Retail BTMG. It is not clear – and 
PJM does not explain – why such units should be categorically excluded from taking 
advantage of the benefits that may be available to co-located generation (subject to the 
associated requirements), which appears to be the result under PJM’s proposal. 
AMP recognizes that an Eligible Customer taking service on behalf of load with 
Non-Retail BTMG may have little incentive to utilize one of the three new types of 
transmission service to the extent that all or a portion of a municipal, cooperative, or 
electric distribution company generator is engaged in netting under the existing Non-
Retail BTMG Tariff provisions. There may be circumstances, however, in which a 
generating facility that qualifies as Non-Retail BTMG might wish to utilize one of the new 
transmission services. For example, section 34.3 of the PJM Tariff caps the total amount 
of Non-Retail BTMG in the PJM Region eligible for netting in any specific year, and sets 
a maximum ceiling of 3,000 MW (unless increased through a section 205 filing).27 If and 
when the netting cap is reached, there may be a greater incentive for generators that 
qualify as Non-Retail BTMG to consider one of the new transmission services. Excluding 
Non-Retail BTMG from this opportunity would frustrate the Commission’s objective of 
making the new transmission service options available to load with BTMG.28
26 See, e.g., PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 173 FERC ¶ 61,244, at P 50 (2020) (explaining that 
“[c]ompliance filings must be limited to the specific directives ordered by the Commission,” and directing 
PJM to remove certain proposed Tariff provisions included in a compliance filing). 
27 See PJM Filing, Attachment A, proposed Tariff, section 34.3; see also December 18 Order at P 222. 
28  June 18 Order at P 91.

7 
Assuming the Commission otherwise accepts PJM’s proposal to add a definition 
of Eligible Generating Facility, AMP proposes the following revised definition in lieu of 
PJM’s proposal to address the concerns described above: 
“Eligible Generating Facility” shall mean a Co-Located 
Generating Facility or Retail Behind the Meter Generation. 
Directing PJM to revise the definition of Eligible Generating Facility is well within 
the Commission’s authority. PJM submitted its filing in this docket pursuant to section 206 
of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”) for the purpose of establishing a just and reasonable 
replacement rate given the Commission’s finding that certain aspects of the existing PJM 
Tariff were unjust, unreasonable, and unduly discriminatory or preferential. The 
Commission has the obligation to fix the just and reasonable replacement rate,29 and it is 
not restricted to accepting or rejecting PJM’s compliance proposal submitted under FPA 
section 206.30
29 See, e.g., 16 U.S.C. § 824e(a); Advanced Energy Mgmt. All. v. FERC, 860 F.3d 656, 663 (D.C. Cir. 
2017) (citation modified) (“When the Commission changes an existing filed rate under section 206, it is 
the Commission’s burden to prove the reasonableness of its change in methodology.”). 
30 See, e.g., Bldg. for the Future Through Elec. Reg’l Transmission Planning and Cost Allocation, Order 
No. 1920-B, 191 FERC ¶ 61,026, at PP 46-51 (2025) (rejecting arguments that compliance filings in a 
FPA section 206 proceeding implicate public utilities’ FPA section 205 filing rights).

8 
III. 
CONCLUSION 
WHEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, American Municipal Power, Inc. 
respectfully requests that the Commission direct PJM to revise its proposed definition of 
Eligible Generating Facility as described herein. 
Respectfully submitted,
